nodes.summary: Fix a base $b \ge 2$ and a natural number $n$. Call $n$ a comma-child of $k$ if $n = k + b\,(k \bmod b) + y$ for some comma candidate digit $y$ of $k$ in base $b$. Let $f$ be the most significant base-$b$ digit of $n$ and let $x = (n - f) \bmod b$. If $n$ is a comma-child of a positive integer $k$, then $k = n - x b - f$; and if the integer $n - x b - f$ is negative, then $n$ is not a comma-child of any positive…
nodes.title: Recovering the parent of a comma-child

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $b$ and $m$, let $k$ be the base-$b$ logarithm of $m$ rounded down, that is, the largest $k$ with $b^k \le m$ when $b \ge 2$ and $m \ge 1$, and $k = 0$ otherwise. The most significant digit of $m$ in base $b$ is $\lfloor m / b^k \rfloor$. When $b \ge 2$ and $m \ge 1$ this is the leading digit of the base-$b$ expansion of $m$.
nodes.title: Most significant digit

nodes.summary: For every base $b$ with $3 \le b \le 633$ and every positive integer $v$, the comma sequence in base $b$ starting at $v$ terminates, that is, there is no infinite comma sequence in base $b$ starting at $v$.
nodes.title: Comma sequences terminate in bases 3 to 633

nodes.summary: Let $b \ge 2$ and $n \ge b^2$. Then there are a positive integer $k$ and a comma candidate digit $y$ of $k$ in base $b$ with $n = k + b\,(k \bmod b) + y$, that is, $n$ is a comma-child of $k$.
nodes.title: Every number at least the square of the base is a comma-child

nodes.summary: For every base $b \ge 2$ there is a sequence $a_0, a_1, \dots$ of positive integers such that for every $i$ there is a comma candidate digit $y$ of $a_i$ in base $b$ with $a_{i+1} = a_i + b\,(a_i \bmod b) + y$, that is, each $a_{i+1}$ is a comma-child of $a_i$.
nodes.title: The comma-child graph has an infinite path

nodes.summary: There is exactly one sequence $a_0, a_1, \dots$ of natural numbers with $a_0 = 1$ such that for every $i$ there is a comma candidate digit $y$ of $a_i$ in base $3$ with $a_{i+1} = a_i + 3\,(a_i \bmod 3) + y$, that is, each $a_{i+1}$ is a base-3 comma-child of $a_i$.
nodes.title: There is a unique infinite comma-child path from 1 in base 3

nodes.summary: Let $b$ and $n$ be natural numbers and let $y$ be a digit with $0 \le y < b$. Put $m = n + b\,(n \bmod b) + y$, where $n \bmod b$ is the remainder of $n$ on division by $b$. Then $y$ is a comma candidate for $n$ in base $b$ if $m > 0$ and the most significant base-$b$ digit of $m$ equals $y$.
nodes.title: Comma candidate digits

nodes.summary: Let $b$, $n$ and $m$ be natural numbers. Then $m$ is the comma successor of $n$ in base $b$ if there is a comma candidate digit $y < b$ for $n$ in base $b$ such that $m = n + b\,(n \bmod b) + y$ and no digit $y' < y$ is a comma candidate for $n$ in base $b$.
nodes.title: Comma successor

nodes.summary: Let $b \ge 2$ and let $n$ be a positive integer. Then no digit $y < b$ is a comma candidate for $n$ in base $b$ (so $n$ has no comma successor) if and only if the base-$b$ representation of $n$, most significant digit first, is $(b-1) \cdots (b-1)\, x\, (b-1-x)$ with some number $i \ge 0$ of leading digits $b - 1$ and $1 \le x \le b - 2$.
nodes.title: Landmines of the comma sequence

nodes.summary: Let $b$ and $n$ be natural numbers. Then $n$ is comma-terminal in base $b$ if no digit $y$ with $0 \le y < b$ is a comma candidate for $n$ in base $b$, so $n$ has no comma successor in base $b$.
nodes.title: Comma-terminal numbers

nodes.summary: Let $b$ and $v$ be natural numbers. The comma sequence in base $b$ starting at $v$ terminates if $b \ge 2$, $v > 0$, and there is no infinite comma sequence in base $b$ starting at $v$.
nodes.title: Terminating comma sequences

nodes.summary: Let $b$ and $v$ be natural numbers and let $a : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ be a sequence. Then $a$ is an infinite comma sequence in base $b$ starting at $v$ if $b \ge 2$, $v > 0$, $a_1 = v$, and for every $n \ge 1$ the term $a_{n+1}$ is the comma successor of $a_n$ in base $b$.
nodes.title: Infinite comma sequences

nodes.summary: Let $b \ge 3$ and $n \ge b^2 - 1$. Then $n$ is not the comma successor in base $b$ of any positive integer if and only if $n = c\, b^i$ for some $i \ge 2$ and some $c$ with $2 \le c \le b - 1$.
nodes.title: Numbers that are not comma successors

nodes.summary: Fix a base $b \ge 2$, and say that $n$ has at least two comma-children if there are distinct digits $y_1 \ne y_2$ below $b$ that are both comma candidates for $n$ in base $b$ (distinct candidates $y$ give distinct children $n + b\,(n \bmod b) + y$). Then a positive integer $n < b^2$ has at least two comma-children if and only if $n = (b - 1 - 2x)\, b + x$ for some $x$ with $1 \le x$ and $2x \le b - 1$; and an…
nodes.title: Numbers with two comma-children

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
